narrative.overview: A quiet, dark workroom where Korean code is the brightest thing on screen. The interface is a working IDE first; the identity lives in a few precise details taken from dancheong: a hairline band of 청·적·황·녹, an indigo primary action, and status colours drawn from the same family.
keyCharacteristics: Terminal-dark surfaces in four steps separated by hairlines.
One primary action per surface: Run, which becomes Stop while a run is live.
Dancheong band at the top edge of the header and the app mark; nowhere else as decoration.
Status is colour + icon + words, never colour alone.
Korean copy first, written for Korean readers.

rules.name: The Meaning-Only Rule
rules.body: Dancheong hues mark state or action. Outside the top band and the mark, a hue that carries no meaning is a bug.

rules.name: The Two-Shade Rule
rules.body: Every accent has a fill shade and a text shade. Never put the fill shade on a dark panel as text.

rules.name: The Lift-Only-When-Floating Rule
rules.body: A shadow means this is above the work and will go away.

dos: Do keep Run the only filled indigo button on the main screen.
Do pair every status colour with an icon and a word.
Do write Korean copy in plain 해요체 for learners, and say what to do next in every error.
Do use the CSS tokens instead of raw colours.
donts: Don't use Tailwind's raw gray/blue palette in components; it ignores the light theme.
Don't use emoji or Unicode glyphs as icons; use lucide icons at 16px.
Don't spread dancheong colours as decoration beyond the top band and the mark.
Don't put text in text-whisper on anything lighter than the raised surface.
